rows.grounds: then the installation of the eight Ghoras
the head consisting of their feet

items.question: What installations follow on the back and head in this sequence?
premises: The three-principle installation is placed on the back reaching the three regions.
Then the installation of the eight Ghoras follows.
The head is constituted by their feet.
items.inference: After the three-principle installation on the back, the rite proceeds to the eight-Ghora installation culminating at the head.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of the three regions and the feet of the eight Ghoras is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: On the back, extending through the three regions, one performs the installation of the three principles. Then comes the installation of the eight Ghoras, with the head formed by their feet.

rows.grounds: installation of the being of Shiva
in this fivefold set, by its primacy
rows.morph: pañcake n.loc.sg + asmin n.loc.sg + yat-tat-mukhyatayā f.ins.sg (compound)

items.question: What determines what is to be worshipped after the fivefold installation is completed?
premises: After that comes the installation of the being of Shiva connected with one's own body.
When this fivefold installation has been performed, primacy within it determines the focus.
The object of worship and ritual attention follows that primacy.
items.inference: Once the fivefold installation is complete, the element that holds primacy within it becomes the main object of worship.
uncertainties: The verse does not explicitly name the worshipped object, which is clarified in the next verse.
items.plain_english: Then comes the installation of the being of Shiva, joined with one's own body. When this fivefold set has been performed, whatever holds primacy within it should become the main focus.

items.question: Who is to be installed and worshipped in the sixth installation?
premises: The object to be contemplated and worshipped, together with its limbs, is placed in the sixth installation.
This placement makes that deity the one fit for installation here.
The deity named is the Lord Ratiśekhara.
items.inference: In the sixth installation, the Lord Ratiśekhara, together with his limbs, is the proper object to be installed and worshipped.
items.plain_english: In the sixth installation, one should place the object of contemplation and worship together with its limbs. Therefore, the Lord Ratiśekhara is the one fit to be installed here.

rows.grounds: of the one called the ninefold
when it is primary, the other has a different abode
when the being of Bhairava is the lord

items.question: How does the placement change when the ninefold or Bhairava-being is given primacy?
premises: The ninefold is to be installed above.
When the ninefold is primary, the other occupies a different abode.
The same principle applies if the being of Bhairava is taken as primary.
items.inference: Primacy determines placement: whichever form is primary is installed in its proper position, and the other is relocated accordingly.
uncertainties: The compound anyonyadhāmatā is read as the other having a different abode; the exact nuance is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The ninefold is to be installed above. When it is given primacy, the other is placed in a different abode. The same rule applies if the being of Bhairava is made primary.

items.question: How was the placement of Ratiśekhara transmitted in the Śrīpūrva tradition?
premises: Ratiśekhara is to be installed beforehand in the respective place according to what is worshipped.
This procedure was expounded in the Śrīpūrva scripture.
The teaching was transmitted to the author as a tradition.
items.inference: The author presents the prior installation of Ratiśekhara in its proper place as a received teaching from the Śrīpūrva tradition.
items.plain_english: Ratiśekhara is to be installed beforehand in the place appropriate to what is being worshipped. This is how the tradition was set forth to me in the Śrīpūrva scripture.

rows.grounds: is excluded in this, and his limbs also
rows.morph: vivarjyate 3.sg.passive (vi-vṛj) + amuṣmin m.loc.sg + aṅgāni n.nom.pl + api (indecl.) + asya m.gen.sg

items.question: Why can the deity not be excluded from the installation procedure?
premises: The Lord Śambhu is the deity in the procedure of installation.
If he were excluded, the installation would lack its basis.
His limbs also exist and belong to that installation.
items.inference: The deity and his limbs are integral to the installation and cannot be omitted.
uncertainties: The vocative nyāsa is slightly abrupt; it may be read as an address within the argument.
items.plain_english: In the procedure of installation, the Lord Śambhu is the deity. How could he be excluded? His limbs also exist and are part of it.

rows.grounds: joined with the form and limbs

items.question: How is the sixfold installation structured in terms of form, limbs, and principles?
premises: The form, emanation, and three principles, together with the form and limbs, make eight components.
Shiva is to be understood together with his limbs.
The installation is declared to be sixfold.
items.inference: The sixfold installation integrates Shiva, his limbs, and the related components of form, emanation, and the three principles.
uncertainties: The exact counting that yields six from the listed components is compressed in the verse.
items.plain_english: The form, emanation, and the three principles, together with the form and limbs, are to be understood as belonging to Shiva with his limbs. The installation is declared to be sixfold.

items.question: What is the first step in the sixfold Shakta installation performed after the previous rite?
premises: After the preceding installation, a sixfold Shakta installation is to be performed.
The sequence begins with Parāparā together with her faces.
Mālinī is also named at the beginning of this sequence.
items.inference: The Shakta installation follows the previous rite as a sixfold sequence beginning with Parāparā and Mālinī.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of prāgiti mālinīm is compressed; it is read as indicating Mālinī at the start.
items.plain_english: Above this, one should then perform the sixfold Shakta installation. First comes Parāparā with her faces, and thus Mālinī at the beginning.

rows.grounds: afterward the triad beginning with Parā
placed at crest, heart, and feet
in the head, face, and throat
from heart, navel, secret place, and thighs

items.question: Where is the triad beginning with Parā installed in the body?
premises: After the first step, the triad beginning with Parā is installed.
It is placed in sequence at the crest, heart, and feet.
The sequence continues through head, face, throat, heart, navel, secret place, and thighs.
items.inference: The triad beginning with Parā is distributed across specific bodily locations in a fixed descending order.
uncertainties: The verse lists locations compactly; the exact assignment of each member of the triad to each location is implied rather than spelled out.
items.plain_english: After that, the triad beginning with Parā is installed in order at the crest, heart, and feet. Then the sequence continues through the head, face, throat, heart, navel, secret place, and thighs.

rows.grounds: also in knee and foot, beginning with Aghorā
the fivefold limbs of the vidyā
then one should invoke the Shakti
whose form is the being of the Mother

items.question: What follows the bodily placements before the invocation of Shakti?
premises: The sequence beginning with Aghorā is placed in the knee and foot.
Then the fivefold limbs of the vidyā are installed.
After that, the Shakti whose form is the being of the Mother is invoked.
items.inference: The rite moves from bodily placements to the vidyā limbs and culminates in invoking the Mother-form Shakti.
items.plain_english: The sequence beginning with Aghorā is placed in the knee and foot. Then come the five limbs of the vidyā. After that, one should invoke the Shakti whose form is the being of the Mother.

rows.grounds: augmented by the twelve Shaktis of limbs, faces, and retinue

items.question: How is the invoked Shakti characterized in this installation?
premises: The invoked Shakti is named as Yogeśvarī, supreme, full, Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, and steadfast.
She is accompanied by twelve Shaktis forming her limbs, faces, and retinue.
These attributes define her presence in the rite.
items.inference: The invoked Shakti is a supreme, complete Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī attended by a twelvefold retinue.
items.plain_english: One invokes Yogeśvarī, the supreme, full, steadfast Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, augmented by the twelve Shaktis of her limbs, faces, and retinue.

rows.grounds: according to the difference of aim and practice
in the middle of the triad of goddesses

items.question: How should the guru contemplate the goddess during installation according to the aim of the rite?
premises: The contemplation varies according to the aim and practice of the rite.
At the time of installation, the guru should remember the goddess.
The supreme goddess abides in the middle of the triad as non-differentiating.
items.inference: Depending on the rite's aim, the guru should contemplate the supreme non-differentiating goddess at the center of the triad.
items.plain_english: At the time of installation, the guru should contemplate according to the aim and practice of the rite. The supreme goddess, abiding in the middle of the triad, is the non-differentiating one.

rows.grounds: she, this being of unlimited consciousness alone
rows.morph: sā f.nom.sg + anavaccheda-cinmātra-sadbhāvā f.nom.sg (compound) + iyam f.nom.sg

items.question: How is the supreme goddess identified in the Sāra and Yāmala scriptures?
premises: The goddess is described as the being of unlimited consciousness alone.
This identification is proclaimed in the Sāra scripture and the Yāmala.
That scriptural identification grounds her form in the rite.
items.inference: The supreme goddess is scripturally identified as pure unlimited consciousness, and this defines her ritual form.
items.plain_english: She is proclaimed as the being of unlimited consciousness alone. This is declared in the Sāra scripture and in the Yāmala, and therefore this is how the goddess is understood.

rows.grounds: the triad of Shaktis and then the eight

items.question: What are the six components of the Shakta installation?
premises: The components include the form with faces and the Shakti.
They also include the triad of Shaktis, the group of eight, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti.
Together these constitute the Shakta installation.
items.inference: The Shakta installation is sixfold, comprising the goddess's form, her Shakti groups, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of the listed groups into six divisions is compactly stated.
items.plain_english: The form with faces, the Shakti, the triad of Shaktis, the group of eight, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti make up the Shakta installation, which is also sixfold.

rows.grounds: granting the fruits of accomplishment and liberation

items.question: How should the great Yāmala installation be adapted for one who seeks only liberation?
premises: This Yāmala great installation grants both accomplishment and liberation.
A practitioner who seeks liberation alone has a different priority.
Such a practitioner should perform the Shakta installation first.
items.inference: For a seeker of liberation alone, the Shakta installation takes precedence within the great Yāmala rite.
items.plain_english: This Yāmala great installation gives the fruits of accomplishment and liberation. But one who seeks liberation alone should first perform the Shakta installation.

rows.grounds: which pair of installations has been stated
rows.morph: yat n.nom.sg + nyāsa-dvayam n.nom.sg (compound) + udāhṛtam n.nom.sg

items.question: How do the gurus instruct a liberation-seeker to perform the two installations?
premises: A pair of installations has been described.
The gurus give a specific instruction for one desiring liberation.
That practitioner should perform the rite beginning with the feet in the order of withdrawal.
items.inference: For a liberation-seeker, the gurus prescribe performing the two installations in reverse, from the feet upward, following the order of withdrawal.
items.plain_english: The gurus say that for one who desires liberation, the pair of installations described should be performed beginning with the feet, in the order of withdrawal.

rows.grounds: denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual

items.question: Does the sixfold installation apply across all mantra divisions of Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual?
premises: There are many divisions denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual.
These divisions appear across various mantras.
The installation is declared to be sixfold in all of them.
items.inference: Regardless of the mantra division, the installation remains sixfold across Śambhu, Shakti, and individual forms.
items.plain_english: However many divisions are declared as denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual, in all those mantras the installation is proclaimed as sixfold.

rows.grounds: but the one to be invoked
this is stated as sixfold alone
rows.morph: ṣoḍhā (indecl.) + eva (indecl.) + ayam m.nom.sg + udāhṛtaḥ m.nom.sg

items.question: What serves as the sixth element in the sixfold installation across all cases?
premises: The mantra that is invoked is endowed with its limbs.
That invoked mantra constitutes the sixth element.
This rule applies in all cases.
items.inference: In every case, the invoked mantra together with its limbs functions as the sixth part of the sixfold installation.
items.plain_english: But the mantra that is invoked, endowed with its limbs, should be the sixth. Thus in all cases this installation is stated as sixfold.

items.question: What ritual and experiential elements follow the installation in this sequence?
premises: Afterward the mudrās are displayed by body, mind, and speech.
There are five states beginning with waking.
A sixth state is named the unsurpassed.
items.inference: The rite continues with mudrā display through body, mind, and speech and culminates in the sixth unsurpassed state beyond the five.
items.plain_english: Afterward come the display of mudrās by body, mind, and speech. There are the five states beginning with waking, and a sixth called the unsurpassed.

rows.grounds: because of six causes and sixfold selfhood, the joining of the thirty-six principles

items.question: What cosmic integration is achieved when the sixfold great installation is performed?
premises: The rite involves six causes, sixfold selfhood, and the joining of the thirty-six principles.
When the sixfold great installation is performed, this integration is enacted.
The whole universe is drawn into that integration.
items.inference: The sixfold great installation integrates the thirty-six principles and powerfully unites the universe within the rite.
uncertainties: The compound ṣaṭkāraṇaṣaḍātmatvāt is dense; the gloss follows the most direct reading.
items.plain_english: Because of the six causes, the sixfold selfhood, and the joining of the thirty-six principles, when the sixfold great installation is performed, this whole universe is powerfully brought into unity.

rows.grounds: beginning from the installation of the form

items.question: How does the emanation begun in the installation become a pure emanation in the body?
premises: The universe attains identity with the body through the rite.
Beginning from the installation of the form, an emanation spreads forth.
That emanation is to be revealed as pure.
items.inference: The emanation initiated by the form-installation is realized in the body as a pure emanation through identity.
items.plain_english: Having attained identity in the body, one should reveal a pure emanation. Beginning from the installation of the form, the emanation that has spread forth here is that pure emanation.

rows.grounds: by the force and sequence of the installation
regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds

items.question: Why is the objection about returning after burning the bonds misplaced?
premises: The emanation is made pure by bringing it to non-difference through the power of installation.
This process concerns the shaking off of the burning of bonds.
Some deluded people object to this process.
items.inference: Because the rite establishes non-difference and purity, objections about reverting after the bonds are burned arise from misunderstanding.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of pāśadāhavidhūnane is compact; it is read as the removal that follows the burning of bonds.
items.plain_english: By the power and order of the installation, the emanation is brought to non-difference and made pure. Therefore those deluded people who object regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds are mistaken.

items.question: What is wrong with asking why one established in peaceful Shiva would descend again?
premises: The objection asks why one established in peaceful Shiva would descend again.
Such an objection assumes a fall from that establishment.
The objectors do not understand the ultimate reality of Śambhu.
items.inference: The objection is refuted because it misunderstands the Śaiva ultimate reality in which establishment in Shiva is not a reversible state.
items.plain_english: When one is established in peaceful Shiva, why would he descend again? Those who ask this are refuted from the outset, for they do not understand the ultimate reality of Śambhu.

rows.grounds: devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness

items.question: Why do the objectors fail to understand the nature of peaceful Shiva?
premises: The objectors are devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness.
Because of this, they do not know the truth.
Peaceful Shiva is not some differentiated entity.
items.inference: Lacking the living essence of self-awareness, the objectors misconceive peaceful Shiva as a differentiated thing.
items.plain_english: They do not know, because they are devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness. For this peaceful Shiva is not some differentiated entity.
